heading: The evidence was preserved. Retrieval still missed part of it.
scope: Our current test follows evidence through a small retrieval system: what was kept, what was returned, and what a question actually required.

requiredText: Complete declared support at 1, 3 and 5 | 5/6 at each cutoff
All six unsupported questions also returned passages.
They omitted the capability-discovery passage, even though that passage survived intact in the indexed representation.
The diagnostic has not executed at this record's cutoff.
The proposal is not an executed experiment.
Two clause queries can return more windows than one whole query.

results.label: Coverage check
results.summary: Two runs reproduced the same result. All six unsupported questions also returned passages; retrieving text does not establish that a question can be answered.

results.label: Gap diagnosis
results.measure: required evidence was indexed, but not returned
results.summary: One question asked about both discovering payment capabilities and committing payment state. The five returned passages omitted the discovery evidence. Review found no complete alternative answer in them.

limits: These are visible development questions over four saved sources. No answers were generated. Predictive advantage, broader entity coverage and the cause of the retrieval ranking remain unmeasured.

next.question: Does asking the two parts separately recover the missing evidence?
next.description: Prepare one fixed diagnostic: capability discovery, then payment commitment, using the same saved sources and raw-text method. Freeze the clauses, run count and stopping rule before retrieving again.
next.budget: Two top-five lists allow up to ten windows, compared with five in the original test. Recovery would show sensitivity to that change, not a fair-budget improvement.
